Working through the constraints gives one valid schedule, the same one as before.

- Gus, Ben, and Hana occupy three consecutive slots starting at g. Elif is before Hana and at least three slots from Ben, so Elif ≤ g−2. Ann < Ivo < Elif then forces g ≥ 5.
- Finn must come after Gus, and slots g+1 and g+2 are taken by Ben and Hana, so g ≤ 6.
- g = 5 fails: Ann, Ivo, and Elif would have to fill slots 1–3, but Dev must then sit right after Ivo, which collides with Elif.
- g = 6 works. Ann 1, Ivo 2, Dev 3, Elif 4, Gus 6, Ben 7, Hana 8. Cara must be 5 or 9, and Finn must come after Elif and Gus, so Finn takes 9 and Cara takes 5.

Checking every constraint against the schedule:
- Ivo (2) before Elif (4) ✓
- |Hana (8) − Ivo (2)| = 6 ≥ 3 ✓
- Ann (1) before Ivo (2) ✓
- Ben (7) immediately after Gus (6) ✓
- Ivo (2) before Cara (5) ✓
- |Ben (7) − Elif (4)| = 3 ≥ 3 ✓
- Hana (8) immediately after Ben (7) ✓
- Elif (4) before Hana (8) ✓
- Ivo (2) before Finn (9) ✓
- Gus (6) before Ben (7) ✓
- Exactly one person between Ben (7) and Cara (5) — Gus is in slot 6 ✓
- Gus (6) before Finn (9) ✓
- Dev (3) immediately after Ivo (2) ✓
- Elif (4) before Finn (9) ✓

The note in my earlier answer, saying Elif is in slot 5 and Cara is in slot 4, is wrong. With Elif in slot 5, |Ben − Elif| = 2, which breaks the three-slot constraint. The correct order is Elif in 4 and Cara in 5.
